title: Signal, Image Processing and Pattern Recognition
abstract: Connected and Autonomous vehicles (CAVs) generate vast amounts of data across sensors, V2X communication channels, and in-vehicle networks, resulting in significant challenges for cybersecurity, forensic analysis, and post-incident inspection.This paper presents a comprehensive review and comparative analysis of existing cyber-forensic systems, secure logging mechanisms, blockchain-based evidence management frameworks, AI-driven threat detection models, and automotive digital forensic methodologies.By investigating research on in-vehicle data integrity, sensor forensics, intrusion detection, privacy-preserving evidence management, and Internet of Vehicles (IoV) forensic readiness, the study identifies several key challenges and research gaps.These include limited real-world validation of proposed solutions, the absence of standardised forensic procedures, scalability limitations in handling large volumes of vehicle-generated data, and insufficient integration among forensic components.In addition, the paper evaluates widely used vehicular diagnostic and penetrationtesting tools to assess their effectiveness and applicability in digital forensic investigations.Based on a synthesis of current literature and existing tool capabilities, the study highlights the growing need for unified, automated, and interoperable forensic architectures capable of supporting large-scale data analysis, tamper-evident evidence management, and comprehensive incident reconstruction across Connected and Autonomous Vehicle (CAV) ecosystems.Such architectures are essential to enhancing forensic readiness, improving cybersecurity resilience, and enabling reliable post-incident investigations in increasingly connected transportation environments.The findings provide a foundation for future research toward scalable, AI-enabled, and standardised cyber-forensic frameworks for next-generation intelligent transportation systems.

title: Verti-WM: A Physics-Aided Exteroceptive World Model for Off-Road Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Reinforcement learning for off-road navigation requires extensive vehicle-terrain interaction data, which are costly to collect in high-fidelity simulation. World models offer a promising alternative by replacing simulator roll-outs during policy optimization. However, an off-road world model must condition state transitions on exteroceptive terrain information, which proprioception alone does not provide. This challenge is further amplified by the need to model both rigid and deformable terrain, where data-driven and physics-based approaches offer complementary strengths. We propose Verti-WM, a physics-aided exteroceptive world model that recurrently fuses a frozen Transformer for rigid terrain and a neuro-symbolic terramechanics model for deformable terrain. Elevation and semantic observations queried from a supplied map at each predicted pose condition fusion, enabling six-degree-of-freedom rollouts for policy optimization without further simulator access. Verti-WM reduces prediction error by 34.6% and 21.7% over data-driven and physics-based baselines, respectively. Policies trained entirely within Verti-WM achieve comparable task success rates while reducing computation time by 23.6X relative to direct training in the high-fidelity simulator. We further validate Verti-WM using real-world data, enabling policy optimization within learned real-world kinodynamics and achieving a 80% success rate on the Verti-4-Wheeler platform, compared with 40% for direct sim-to-real transfer.

title: Multi-Armed Bernoulli Bandits via Minimax Single-Arm Stopping
abstract: We develop an index policy for finite-horizon Bernoulli multi-armed bandits from minimax solutions to single-arm bandit (SAB) problems. Each SAB problem involves choosing between an unknown Bernoulli arm and a known reward. We show that minimizing worst-case regret of SAB problems over all non-anticipative policies admits an exact semi-infinite linear programming formulation. The resulting stopping policies offer a natural way to compare arms: the higher the known reward against which a policy continues sampling, the more promising the unknown arm. We turn this intuition into indices based on cumulative continuation probabilities, with a monotone adjustment and a reward-shortfall cap. By relating index errors to the regret of single-arm stopping policies, we establish a distribution-free regret bound of $4.45\sqrt{KT}+10.75K$ for $K$ arms and horizon $T$. This bound matches the minimax-optimal regret order established in the literature. The guarantee extends to rewards supported on $[0,1]$ through Bernoulli randomization. We also provide a finite-grid implementation with quantified approximation loss. In numerical experiments, the SAB-based index policy achieves lower worst-case regret than every tested benchmark policy across all evaluated numbers of arms and horizons, while closely matching the grid-based MAB minimax policy in the two-arm setting.

title: EXODUS: An Explicit Outcome-Driven Uncertainty Screening Controller for Diffusion Language Model Sampling
abstract: Masked diffusion language models can revise committed tokens to correct errors at the cost of additional computation. Because recovery benefits vary across tokens and denoising steps, fixed policies can spend this computation on unhelpful revisions. We present EXplicit Outcome-Driven Uncertainty Screening (EXODUS), a method that selects recovery requests using commitment confidence and denoising progress. EXODUS rejects high-confidence or late requests using existing sampler information while preserving scheduled denoising. We derive sufficient conditions for both decisions by relating the expected benefit of recovery to its computational cost. Experiments with LLaDA and Dream on GSM8K, HumanEval, and MBPP compare EXODUS against four baselines. The results show that EXODUS provides competitive quality--latency tradeoffs while reducing the latency and forward-pass cost of optional recovery.

title: Evidential Post-Clustering Explanations with Dempster–Shafer Surrogates
abstract: Post-clustering explanations connect unsupervised partitions to explicit rules describing cluster membership. We present a modular empirical evaluation framework that jointly assesses surrogate fidelity, partition validity, explanation complexity, and uncertainty across hard, fuzzy, and evidential clustering outputs. K-Means, Agglomerative Clustering, DBSCAN, Fuzzy C-Means, and Evidential C-Means are paired with Decision Tree, RIPPER, and Dempster-Shafer Gradient Descent (DSGD) surrogates on synthetic, tabular, digit-image, biological, and text representations. Learnability and non-leaky protocols distinguish reproduction of a full-data partition from evaluation with clustering fitted on training data. Native fuzzy and evidential diagnostics complement fidelity to hardened assignments, while the DSGD maximum-score-based ambiguity proxy provides an epistemic diagnostic. In the common six-dataset benchmark, shallow Decision Trees achieve the highest average hard-label fidelity for K-Means, Agglomerative Clustering, Fuzzy C-Means, and Evidential C-Means. For DBSCAN, macro-F1 and noise diagnostics further characterize agreement with imbalanced cluster assignments. Joint analysis of membership entropy and fidelity distinguishes reproduction of hardened labels from membership concentration. The framework provides a reproducible basis for selecting and assessing clustering-surrogate pairings according to partition geometry, output type, and explanation requirements.

title: Использование космической информации в комплексе с наземными геологическими исследованиями на территории Восточного Кавказа
abstract: Актуальность работы. Использование космической информации в разведочной геологии значительно повышает эффективность наземных геологических методов поиска месторождений различных полезных ископаемых. Особую роль и значимость приобретает использование космической информации на труднодоступных участках земной поверхности, таких как восточно-кавказский сегмент сооружения Большого Кавказа. Цель исследования. Анализ использования космической информации в выявлении и прослеживании дизъюнктивных нарушений и шовных зон в фундаменте и осадочном чехле региона, кольцевых структур, линеаментов и тектонических блоков различного уровня. Методы исследования. Основными методами исследования являются дешифрирование космических снимков, морфотектонический анализ, структурно-геоморфологический анализ, использование результатов тепловой съемки, а также анализ материалов геофизических исследований и бурения. Результаты исследования. В результате проведенных исследований дешифрированы крупные кольцевые структуры, такие как Терско-Кумская, Сулакская, морфоструктуры центрального типа (Верхнеандийская, Цурибская и Аргунская), которые в современный период являются активными, а также Хадумский купол, Талгинский свод и малые кольцевые структуры – Акушинская, Мекегинская. Применение космической информации совместно с наземными геологическими методами позволило выявить сеть дизъюнктивных нарушений, детализировать представления о тектоническом строении региона. Выделены крупные тектонические структуры, в том числе кольцевые структуры центрального типа, сдвиги и линеаменты Relevance. The use of space information in exploration geology significantly increases the efficiency of ground-based geological methods for searching for deposits of various minerals. The use of space information in hard-to-reach areas of the Earth's surface, such as the Eastern Caucasus segment of the Greater Caucasus structure, plays a particularly important role. Aim. Analysis of the use of space information in identifying and tracing disjunctive faults and seam zones in the basement and sedimentary cover of the region, circular structures, lineaments, and tectonic blocks of various levels. Methods. The main research methods include remote sensing, morphotectonic analysis, structural-geomorphological analysis, the use of thermal imaging results, and the analysis of geophysical and drilling data. Results. As a result of the conducted research, large ring structures such as the Tersko-Kumskaya, Sulakskaya, and central-type morph structures such as the Verkhneandiyskaya, Tsuribskaya, and Argunskaya, which are active in the modern period, as well as the Khadumsky dome, the Talginsky vault, and small ring structures such as the Akushinskaya and Mekeginskaya, have been deciphered. The use of space information in conjunction with ground-based geological methods has made it possible to identify a network of disjunctive faults and to detail the tectonic structure of the region. Major tectonic structures have been identified, including central-type ring structures, thrusts, and lineaments

title: The social presence of artificial intelligence in the MICE industry: Conceptualization, scale development, and validation
abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping the meeting, incentives, conferences and events industry which forms part of the broader tourism industry. Social presence is a central construct in human-artificial intelligence interaction research, yet its conceptualization and measurement remain underdeveloped in this context. This study conceptualizes social presence in artificial intelligence-enabled meeting, incentives, conferences and events services and develops an initial context-specific scale. Following a three-stage scale-development procedure, 362 questionnaires were distributed in China and 300 valid responses were retained for analysis. The scale was refined through literature-based item generation, expert evaluation, pilot feedback, item analysis, and exploratory factor analysis. To strengthen measurement assessment, the revised scale further clarifies content validity, face validity, construct validity, convergent validity, and preliminary discriminant validity. The final scale supports a four-dimensional structure comprising artificial intelligence competence in the meeting, incentives, conferences and events industry, human-like interaction of artificial intelligence, artificial intelligence emotional influence, and artificial intelligence communication accessibility.

title: A Compact Stance-Indexed Anterior-Posterior COP Representation for Parkinson's Disease Classification from Plantar VGRF
abstract: Parkinson's disease alters gait and bilateral coordination, but machine-learning performance also depends on how continuous gait signals are represented. This study investigates whether preserving anterior-posterior center-of-pressure (AP-COP) information at fixed locations across normalized stance provides a compact and informative representation of plantar-force gait signals. Bilateral vertical ground reaction force recordings from 165 participants in the Gait in Parkinson's Disease Database were evaluated using repeated fully nested participant-level cross-validation. We propose AP-COP10, comprising AP-COP position and bilateral asymmetry across five stance windows. AP-COP10 achieved an AUC of 0.894 and outperformed three harmonized literature-derived COP representations under the same evaluation pipeline. The complementary 25 non-AP-COP descriptors alone achieved an AUC of 0.856, while the complete 35-feature representation achieved 0.908. Removing AP-COP10 from the complete representation produced a statistically supported loss in discrimination, whereas adding the complementary descriptors to AP-COP10 yielded only a small, unsupported improvement. Feature competition indicated that the most informative stance-indexed descriptors were concentrated in early and early-mid stance, while source-study holdout and sensor-perturbation analyses supported the robustness of the representation. These findings indicate that stance-indexed AP-COP retains discriminative information that is not readily recovered by broader engineered gait descriptors, supporting compact and interpretable representations for machine-learning analysis of pathological gait.

title: Vision2CAD: A Visual Agent Harness for Explicit Geometry Referencing and Localization in Parametric CAD Modeling
abstract: Generating parametric CAD models requires accurate geometry and stable feature dependencies. Existing methods face challenges in selecting geometric references, interpreting sketch-plane local coordinates, and establishing sketch constraints to projected external geometry. We present Vision2CAD, a visual agent harness that combines vision-language model (VLM) reasoning with deterministic CAD kernel operations. An ID-based interface supports explicit geometry selection, a local-coordinate bridge converts view coordinates into sketch coordinates, and projected-edge localization supports external sketch constraints. These mechanisms establish feature dependencies within the supported modeling operations and constraint types. We also introduce the Geometry Explicit Reference Dataset (GERD), which aligned commands, geometry states and IDs at every modeling step. On GERD-EVL and a DeepCAD test subset, Vision2CAD improves mIoU by 11.1\% and 5.6\% and reduces Chamfer distance by 17.3\% and 41.8\%, respectively. Parameter-editing experiments and ablation studies further proved the preservation of parametric dependencies.

title: HYBRID CRYPTOGRAPHIC FRAMEWORKS FOR SECURE TELEMEDICINE: A SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW
abstract: Telemedicine has transformed healthcare delivery by enabling remote consultations, electronic health record management, and real-time patient monitoring. However, the exchange of sensitive medical information across distributed networks raises significant security and privacy concerns, particularly with the emergence of quantum computing. This systematic literature review examines cryptographic approaches for securing telemedicine systems, focusing on classical cryptography, post-quantum cryptography, hybrid cryptographic frameworks, authentication mechanisms, and context-aware security. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, 45 studies were systematically selected and synthesized. The review reveals a shift from conventional cryptographic methods toward hybrid and quantum-resistant solutions, with CRYSTALS-Kyber and ECC–Kyber emerging as the dominant approaches. It further identifies the limited integration of context aware mechanisms into hybrid cryptographic frameworks as a key research gap. The findings highlight adaptive hybrid cryptography as a promising direction for secure, scalable, and quantum-resistant telemedicine systems.

title: Lee-Yang preserving quantum Markov semigroups and channels
abstract: This preprint studies quantum Markov dynamics and quantum channels that preserve the Lee–Yang property. For systems of two or more qubits, preservation for all Lee–Yang density matrices forces tensor-product dynamics, with local generators characterized by explicit semidefinite conditions. This ordinary preservation property is equivalent to preservation in the presence of arbitrary inert reference systems. For systems containing higher spins, preservation of all pure Lee–Yang inputs excludes intersite interactions and forces isotropic diffusion with axial drift at higher-spin sites. The paper also develops classifications of static maps with stable full Choi tensors, including singular one-qubit maps and independently covariant maps between finite spins, and establishes quantitative rigidity results for diagonal Hamiltonians. The proofs combine positivity of quantum maps, polynomial root-collision arguments, and coherent tensor contraction. The manuscript includes a disclosure of the AI tools used in its development.

title: The Deterministic Mind: A Discipline for Composable Frozen Nodes
abstract: In an AI landscape dominated by trillion-parameter foundation models, The Frozen Mind: Small, Locked, Typed Nodes for Reliable Agentic AI Workflows and the New World of AI Agents makes a provocative argument: production agentic AI demands the opposite discipline. Where the foundation-model paradigm relies on prompt interpretation and stochastic composition, SNAIL — the Single Node Activated Inference Layer — proposes frozen, single-pass neural primitives composed into statically-validated typed dataflow programs with explicit out-of-distribution routing and structured manifest emission. This book is the architecture, the lineage, and the proof. It is a technical manual for engineers, a research synthesis for academics, and a roadmap for anyone building the next generation of reliable AI systems. Drawing on 113 high-caliber sources across six research clusters — frozen neural primitives, OOD detection, typed dataflow, agent reliability, synthetic data, and the SLM-vs-LLM economic argument — the book traces a 40-year lineage from Hughes' "Why Functional Programming Matters" through TensorFlow graph mode, Apache Beam, and AWS Step Functions, arriving at the conclusion that the agentic AI era needs the same discipline that gave us reliable databases and compilers: pure functions, typed composition, immutable outputs, and structured traces. The book ships alongside the SNAIL package on PyPI (pip install snail-dsl), with five runnable example programs covering customer support, invoice processing, email triage, ML training, and image classification. Whether you're an ML practitioner evaluating the SLM revolution, an agent systems architect fighting prompt drift, or a researcher tracing the convergence of functional programming and neural network design, this book gives you the framework, the code, and the citations to build the next generation of agentic AI on solid ground.

title: PanoSeg3R: Feed-Forward 3D Semantic Segmentation for Panoramic Images with an Automatic Data Curation Pipeline
abstract: We present PanoSeg3R, a feed-forward framework for 3D panoramic semantic segmentation. Unlike existing methods designed for perspective inputs, PanoSeg3R jointly predicts 3D geometry and multi-view semantic segmentation in one single forward pass. Built upon a pretrained reconstruction backbone that supports panoramic images, our approach extends feed-forward 3D reconstruction with a query-based mask decoder. Furthermore, we introduce an automatic panorama data curation pipeline that leverages the complementary strengths of off-the-shelf foundation models to generate reliable pseudo semantic annotations, substantially expanding the training data and improving zero-shot generalization. PanoSeg3R achieves state-of-the-art performance on panoramic 3D semantic segmentation, improving 3D mIoU by up to 16.02 on ScanNet++, while the curated training data further improves zero-shot performance by up to 4.26 and 43.28 mIoU on Stanford2D3D and ToF-360, respectively. Website: https://harryyoon777.github.io/PanoSeg3R/

title: A PERSONA-GROUNDED MOBILE SYSTEM TO SUPPORT ADOLESCENT DECISION-MAKING THROUGH SIMULATED HISTORICAL CONVERSATION USING LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS
abstract: Adolescents increasingly bring important life decisions to general-purpose AI chatbots that offer generic advice with no historical grounding, no diversity of perspective, and inconsistent safety behavior for a minor-facing context. This project presents SageCircle, a Flutter mobile application that conditions a large language model on hand-curated biographies of 77 historical figures so that users can discuss real dilemmas with historically anchored “sages,” compare perspectives across a four-figure “Council of Sages,” and journal reflections entirely on-device [3]. Every user message passes through a fail-open moderation gate before reaching the model. Two experiments evaluated the resulting blind spots: a 160- message moderation test found strong detection of direct self-harm language but a recall gap on indirect, teen-voiced phrasing, and a 360-response persona test found that two of six sages exceeded their instructed reply to length on emotionally complex prompts [4]. Compared against persona-conditioned dialogue, scripted therapy chatbots, and memory-based generative agents, SageCircle trades infrastructure weight for biographical grounding and multi-perspective, mobile-friendly reasoning

title: Thin-film lithium niobate-based sensing-computing integrated photonic chip for microwave frequency discrimination
abstract: Real-time and accurate identification of microwave frequencies is of great significance for applications such as radar detection, electronic countermeasures, and future 6G wireless communications. Traditional electronic chip-based frequency discrimination schemes face severe challenges in power consumption and cost when achieving ultra-wide bandwidths, making it difficult to meet the urgent demand for ultra-wideband in applications like 6G. Based on thin-film lithium niobate photonic integration technology, this paper proposes and experimentally demonstrates a sensing-computing integrated microwave frequency discrimination photonic chip, aiming to achieve real-time microwave frequency identification in the optical domain. Firstly, the microwave signal is converted into an optical signal via an on-chip thin-film lithium niobate electro-optic modulator, and then utilizes a disordered microring lattice to construct a photonic reservoir. The incident light carrying the microwave signal information undergoes complex resonance and interference effects, mapping it into a high-dimensional optical response, thereby achieving ultra-low-power, high-speed nonlinear feature extraction at the physical layer. This architecture significantly reduces reliance on high-speed analog-to-digital converters and subsequent electronic processors. Experimental results show that the device achieves single-shot real-time frequency identification over an ultra-wide microwave frequency range from 10 MHz to 66.01 GHz, with a root mean square error of 40 MHz. Furthermore, a multi-tone signal classification and recognition task was performed, achieving an accuracy of 95%. The scheme proposed in this paper provides an efficient new approach for real-time ultra-wideband microwave frequency measurement and has potential in fields such as microwave photonic signal analysis, real-time spectrum sensing, and on-chip intelligent photonic information processing.

title: External validation of AI assisted colposcopy using WHO dataset for cervical precancer and cancer detection
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-guided colposcopy has previously been developed to assist colposcopists in detecting cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse (CIN2+) and guiding biopsies, but internal testing of the AI model could overestimate diagnostic performance. We validated the performance of the AI-guided colposcopy on an independent WHO open-source set of 187 patients with 855 colposcopic images. Forty-five colposcopists with different levels of experience from 12 regions in China participated in the validation set. The sensitivity of the AI system on CIN2+ standalone diagnosis were 84.2% (95%CI 74.4–90.7%). With AI assistance, colposcopists sensitivity increased from 84.8% (95% CI, 82.7–86.9%) to 90.6% (95% CI, 88.7–92.1%). The improvement was most evident among low-experienced colposcopists, with sensitivity increasing by 6.5%, and AUC from 0.72 (95% CI, 0.68–0.77) to 0.76 (95% CI, 0.72–0.80; p = 0.043). AI-guided biopsy support was also associated with a reduction in the mean number of biopsies per case, from 2.48 to 2.02. These findings highlight the AI system’s robust performance on an independent external dataset and its capacity to bridge the diagnostic experience gap among readers, supporting its clinical implementation as a valuable adjunct for colposcopic assessment.

title: RPA: Residual Patch-Token Adapter for Image Retrieval from EEG and MEG
abstract: Most existing MEG and EEG (M/EEG) visual decoding methods align brain signals with a single global embedding extracted from a pretrained visual encoder, leaving open whether intermediate patch representations, which preserve richer and more granular rich visual information, can improve representation learning. To address this question, we introduce the Residual Patch Adapter (RPA), a lightweight, modular adapter that leverages all patch tokens from an intermediate layer of a ViT visual encoder for alignment. Through extensive ablation analyses, we first show that pooling or masking patch tokens degrades the learned representation, demonstrating that retaining the full set of patch tokens is important for EEG alignment, while the CLS token provides little unique information. We then use a series of six quantitative feature analyses to show that both higher-level semantics and lower-level visual features, including color and texture, are essential for this EEG-to-image alignment. Under current protocols, our system achieves Top-1 accuracies of 95.4\% within-subject and 35.5\% cross-subject on THINGS-EEG2, and 65.2\% and 6.7\%, respectively, on THINGS-MEG, achieving state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance across both datasets. Evaluations with alternative brain encoders, including pretrained EEG foundation models, demonstrate that the approach extends beyond the projection-based EEG encoder. Furthermore, we provide a plug-and-play interface that allows RPA to be replaced by convolution, attention, or ConvNeXt alternatives. Together, these findings provide significant insight into M/EEG-to-image representation learning by establishing design principles for leveraging the latent space of visual encoders, and open new directions for brain--image alignment and non-invasive brain--computer interface (BCI).

title: Where to Decide: Control-Plane Geometry in Coherence-Limited Quantum Networks
abstract: Quantum networks are usually framed by two hardware limits: how fast entanglement can be heralded, and how long a memory can hold it. We establish a third, geometric limit: entanglement decoheres while control information travels, so the distance to whoever allocates resources enters the fidelity budget directly. We develop a functional-graph abstraction weighting each link by its predicted multiplicative contribution to end-to-end fidelity, separating global but delayed state from local and immediate state, and compare centralized against local allocation in a replicated discrete-event model. Centralized delivery latency grows with network diameter while local latency is nearly scale invariant, differing up to twenty-fold for short-range traffic; the coherence threshold at which a global view outweighs a fresh one does not shift across the tested sizes; and as heralding accelerates, the dominant cost moves into the control plane. Slot synchronization instead obeys the product of slot rate and one-way link delay, so it is bounded by repeater spacing rather than diameter. Controller placement, decision locality, repeater spacing and slot rate are physical design parameters, not implementation details.

evidence.title: Where to Decide: Control-Plane Geometry in Coherence-Limited Quantum Networks
evidence.abstract: Quantum networks are limited by how fast entanglement can be heralded and how long a memory can hold it. In this paper, we argue that a second limit, purely geometric, is already comparable in severity. Since entanglement decoheres while control decisions are in flight, the distance to whoever makes the decision enters the fidelity budget directly. We introduce a functional graph abstraction in which every entanglement link carries a weight equal to its predicted contribution to end-toendfidelity, and we use it to compare centralised and locally decided allocation in a replicated discrete-event model. Four results follow. With centralised allocation, delivery latency grows with network diameter while with local allocation, latency is scale invariant, giving ratios from four to twenty. The coherence time at which a global view becomes worth more than a fresh one is identical across every network size we tested, making it a property of the hardware rather than of the network. In a large network, the control plane consumes up to ninety-four per cent of the delivery budget, against under six per cent for local decisions. Distributed slot synchronisation is limited by adifferent geometric scale, the repeater spacing, and collapses onto a single curve in the product of slot rate and link delay. Controller placement and slot rate should be treated as physical design parameters, not implementation details.

title: CLEAR: Complex Learned Explicit Analytical Regularization for Ultra-Accelerated 4D Flow CMR Reconstruction
abstract: While compressed-sensing regularizers enable interpretable reconstruction of 4D Flow CMR through transparent variational objectives, their hand-crafted nature is too restrictive under high acceleration. State-of-the-art learning-based approaches mitigate this, but typically encode regularization implicitly through unrolled network modules, which limits their interpretability. To address this limitation, we propose CLEAR, designed to combine the interpretability of compressed sensing with the flexibility of learned models. To the best of our knowledge, it is the first learned regularizer for a 4D reconstruction task. In the ultra-accelerated \(10\times\)--\(50\times\) regime of the CMRx4DFlow2026 challenge, CLEAR outperforms compressed sensing locally low-rank (LLR) and the popular variational network FlowVN, while using less than 10k parameters and preserving an interpretable regularization structure.

title: ClozeCongruence: Human-Style Essay Classification vs. AI-Written Text via Multi-Horizon Semantic Infilling and Calibrated Stylometric Manifolds
abstract: Abstract—Distinguishing authentic human-authored essays from machine-generated prose remains a critical challenge for educational integrity, admissions authenticity, and digital forensics. Existing zero-shot detectors either rely on inaccessible white-box token logits (DetectGPT, Fast-DetectGPT) or penalize formal, non-native human writing styles through uncalibrated perplexity metrics. Furthermore, prior forensic benchmarks frequently evaluate specialized technical preprints (e.g., ArXiv, PeerRead) or truncate samples to 200 words, destroying macro-discursive structure. In this paper, we present ClozeCongruence, an unconfounded forensic framework evaluated on a curated benchmark of $N = 6{,}997$ samples dedicated to full-length human-style essay classification vs. AI-written text (mean length $\approx 640$ words, up to 1,500 words). Our methodology delivers five core contributions under strict zero-target-leakage protocols (verified via label permutation tests yielding null AUROCs of $0.4870 \approx 0.50 \pm 0.02$ and Pearson length correlation $r = 0.0000$): In-Domain Essay Classification & Operating Points: On clean, prompt-matched human vs. machine essays ($N = 3{,}000$; 1,500 matched pairs), zero-shot stylometric scoring achieves an AUROC of 0.8554 [95% Bootstrap CI: 0.8420–0.8682] and AUPRC of 0.8391. To guarantee that 99% of algorithmic accusations are accurate (False Positive Rate $\le 1.0\%$ at threshold $\tau = 0.9276$), zero-shot sensitivity yields a True Positive Rate (TPR) of 13.33% ($\approx 1$ out of 7 AI essays), rising to 39.73% TPR at 5.0% FPR ($\tau = 0.8505$). Augmented by a 5-fold cross-validated supervised manifold ensemble, discrimination reaches an AUROC of 0.9651 with 52.17% TPR at 1.0% FPR. Adversarial Robustness (RAID Benchmark): Across the Full RAID 11-Attack Adversarial Benchmark ($N = 6{,}000$; Dugan et al., ACL 2024), pre-inference canonicalization neutralizes surface attacks: homoglyph substitution recovers from 0.6793 to 0.9649 AUROC ($\Delta = +0.2856$, 62.4% TPR at 1% FPR; clean baseline maintains 0.9799 AUROC). Concurrently, it establishes the empirical failure boundary against 11B DIPPER neural paraphrasing (0.6956 AUROC, 13.2% TPR at 1% FPR; overall benchmark AUROC = 0.9459). Cross-Domain & Zero-Shot Multilingual Transfer (M4): Evaluation on the M4 Benchmark ($N = 4{,}000$ across 8 strata and 6 languages) demonstrates robust generalization on structured academic English (PeerRead AUROC = 0.9977, 92.0% TPR at 1% FPR) alongside natural script attenuation across Arabic (0.8706), German (0.8008), Chinese (0.7143), Urdu (0.7038), and Russian (0.6700) without language-specific tuning (Full M4 AUROC = 0.8165). Boundary Detection & the Slack Window Paradox: On the Chimeric Co-Authorship Benchmark ($N = 2{,}000$ documents), we expose the Slack Window Paradox: while naive $\pm 1$ paragraph slack inflates boundary F1 to 77.35%, heuristic inter-paragraph difference alone yields an AUROC of only 51.32% (random chance). This establishes that short-document slack is an empirical artifact and demonstrates that supervised sliding-window gradient segmentation is required. Attribution Auditing & Demographic Fairness: Cross-architecture fingerprinting achieves 80.01% Macro-F1 across distinct generator families (BLOOMZ, Cohere, GPT), whereas stylometrics collapse into majority prediction ($\text{F1} = 48.03\%$) on intra-family shared-weight variants (ChatGPT vs. GPT-3.5-Turbo). Crucially, the detector achieves a 0.00% False Accusation Rate across $N = 600$ non-native ESL essays at the calibrated 1.0% FPR threshold ($\tau = 0.9276$), deliberately trading sensitivity for equity. All code and curated benchmarks are available at: https://huggingface.co/datasets/DebdipCS/human-vs-ai-essay-benchmark. Index Terms—AI Text Forensics, Human-Style Essay Classification, Multi-Horizon Cloze Infilling, Stylometric Manifolds, RAID Benchmark, Operational Sensitivity.

Our methodology delivers five core contributions under strict zero-target-leakage protocols (verified via label permutation tests yielding null AUROCs of $0.4870 \approx 0.50 \pm 0.02$ and Pearson length correlation $r = 0.0000$): In-Domain Essay Classification & Operating Points: On clean, prompt-matched human vs. machine essays ($N = 3{,}000$; 1,500 matched pairs), zero-shot stylometric scoring achieves an AUROC of 0.8554 [95% Bootstrap CI: 0.8420–0.8682] and AUPRC of 0.8391. To guarantee that 99% of algorithmic accusations are accurate (False Positive Rate $\le 1.0\%$ at threshold $\tau = 0.9276$), zero-shot sensitivity yields a True Positive Rate (TPR) of 13.33% ($\approx 1$ out of 7 AI essays), rising to 39.73% TPR at 5.0% FPR ($\tau = 0.8505$). Augmented by a 5-fold cross-validated supervised manifold ensemble, discrimination reaches an AUROC of 0.9651 with 52.17% TPR at 1.0% FPR. Adversarial Robustness (RAID Benchmark): Across the Full RAID 11-Attack Adversarial Benchmark ($N = 6{,}000$; Dugan et al., ACL 2024), pre-inference canonicalization neutralizes surface attacks: homoglyph substitution recovers from 0.6793 to 0.9649 AUROC ($\Delta = +0.2856$, 62.4% TPR at 1% FPR; clean baseline maintains 0.9799 AUROC). Concurrently, it establishes the empirical failure boundary against 11B DIPPER neural paraphrasing (0.6956 AUROC, 13.2% TPR at 1% FPR; overall benchmark AUROC = 0.9459). Cross-Domain & Zero-Shot Multilingual Transfer (M4): Evaluation on the M4 Benchmark ($N = 4{,}000$ across 8 strata and 6 languages) demonstrates robust generalization on structured academic English (PeerRead AUROC = 0.9977, 92.0% TPR at 1% FPR) alongside natural script attenuation across Arabic (0.8706), German (0.8008), Chinese (0.7143), Urdu (0.7038), and Russian (0.6700) without language-specific tuning (Full M4 AUROC = 0.8165). Boundary Detection & the Slack Window Paradox: On the Chimeric Co-Authorship Benchmark ($N = 2{,}000$ documents), we expose the Slack Window Paradox: while naive $\pm 1$ paragraph slack inflates boundary F1 to 77.35%, heuristic inter-paragraph difference alone yields an AUROC of only 51.32% (random chance). This establishes that short-document slack is an empirical artifact and demonstrates that supervised sliding-window gradient segmentation is required. Attribution Auditing & Demographic Fairness: Cross-architecture fingerprinting achieves 80.01% Macro-F1 across distinct generator families (BLOOMZ, Cohere, GPT), whereas stylometrics collapse into majority prediction ($\text{F1} = 48.03\%$) on intra-family shared-weight variants (ChatGPT vs. GPT-3.5-Turbo). Crucially, the detector achieves a 0.00% False Accusation Rate across $N = 600$ non-native ESL essays at the calibrated 1.0% FPR threshold ($\tau = 0.9276$), deliberately trading sensitivity for equity. All code and curated benchmarks are available at: https://huggingface.co/datasets/DebdipCS/human-vs-ai-essay-benchmark. title: Морфометрический анализ Донецкого складчатого сооружения в связи с проблемой рудоносности
abstract: Актуальность работыопределяется важностью изучения взаимосвязи морфометрических особенностей рельефа Донецкого складчатого сооружения (ДСС) в связи с размещением месторождений и рудопроявлений золота и цветных металлов, что составит научно-методическую основу применения морфометрических методов исследования при прогнозировании и поисках слепых и погребённых рудных скоплений. Цель исследования: выявить морфометрические особенности рельефа ДСС в связи с особенностями геологического строения, неотектоники и пространственным размещением золотого и полиметаллического оруденения. Методы исследования: морфотектонический анализ на основе цифровых моделей рельефа (ЦМР) Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM3) с разрешением пикселя в 90 м, использование математических методов обработки с применением программного комплекса ArcGIS ArcMap 10.4 с установленной лицензией ArcInfo плавающей версии и вспомогательным модулем гидрологической направленности «ArcHydroTools». Результаты исследования: Осуществлён морфотектонический анализ цифровой модели рельефа дневной поверхности Донецкого складчатого сооружения. Построены карты изовершинных и изобазисных поверхностей на основе анализа долин 1-го, 2-го, 3-го, 4-го и 5-го порядков, а также карты глубины эрозионного расчленения (энергии) рельефа соответствующих пяти порядков. На картах энергии рельефа, отстроенных по долинам 1-го порядка с изолиниями отдельно через 10 м и отдельно через 25 м, впервые для Донбасса выделено относительно слабо выраженное, слегка вытянутое в запад-северо-западном направлении куполовидное неотектоническое поднятие. В его пределах выделены три расположенные концентрически геоморфологические зоны. Приуроченность всех известных в Донбассе проявлений интрузивного магматизма, месторождений и рудопроявлений цветных металлов и золота к выделенному поднятию позволяет предполагать, что выявленная глубинная неоднородность может представлять собой проекцию активизированного в неогене мантийного плюма, вызвавшего в мезозое появление обширной области проявления рудно-магматических систем в нижних горизонтах земной коры Донбасса. Вытянутость вдоль оси поднятия рудных районов и узлов может быть связана с условиями транспортировки и разгрузки рудоносных растворов по Персиановскому, Сулино-Константиновскому и другим глубинным разломам. Формирование неотектонического поднятия обеспечило в различных его геоморфологических зонах выведение на дневную поверхность разных уровней рудно-магматической колонны золото-полиметаллического оруденения: надрудного в краевой, рудного в промежуточной и подрудного в центральной The relevance of the work is determined by the importance of studying the relationship of morphometric features of the relief of the Donetsk folded structure (DFS) in connection with the placement of deposits and ore occurrences of gold and non-ferrous metals, which will form the scientific and methodological basis for the use of morphometric research methods in predicting and searching for blind and buried ore accumulations. The aim of the study: to identify the morphometric features of the DFS relief in connection with the features of the geological structure, neotectonics and spatial placement of gold and polymetallic mineralization. Methods: morphotectonic analysis based on digital terrain models (DTM) Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM3) with a pixel resolution of 90 m, the use of mathematical processing methods using the ArcGIS ArcMap 10.4 software complex with an installed ArcInfo floating version license and an auxiliary hydrological module “ArcHydroToolsˮ. Results. Morphotectonic analysis of the digital model of the relief of the day surface of the Donetsk folded structure was carried out. Maps of isoversical and isobase surfaces were constructed based on the analysis of valleys of the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th orders, as well as maps of the depth of erosion dissection (energy) of the relief of the corresponding five orders. On the relief energy maps, rebuilt along the 1st order valleys with isolines separately after 10 m and separately after 25 m, for the first time for Donbas, a relatively weakly expressed, slightly elongated to the west-north-west direction, dome-shaped neotectonic uplift was identified. Within its boundaries, three concentrically located geomorphological zones are distinguished. The coincidence of all the manifestations of intrusive magmatism, deposits and ore occurrences of non-ferrous metals and gold known in Donbas to the identified uplift suggests that the identified deep heterogeneity may be a projection of the mantle plume activated in the Neogene, which caused the appearance of a vast area of the manifestation of ore-magmatic systems in the lower horizons of the Earth’s crust of Donbas in the Mesozoic. The elongation along the axis of the uplift of ore areas and nodes can be associated with the conditions for transporting and unloading ore-bearing solutions along the Persianovsky, Sulino-Konstantinovsky and other deep faults. The formation of a neotectonic uplift ensured in its various geomorphological zones the bringing to the daytime surface of different levels of the ore-magmatic column of gold-polymetallic mineralization: ore in the marginal, ore in the intermediate and ore in the central

title: Earthquake Seismogram Denoising Across Time, Time‐Frequency, and Hybrid Domain Approaches
abstract: Abstract Deep learning earthquake signal denoisers commonly operate directly on waveform data or on time‐frequency representations, yet the impact of this design choice has not been systematically assessed under controlled conditions. Here we design and benchmark four comparable deep learning architectures to assess the effect of input data representation: a time‐domain denoiser, a time‐frequency denoiser–the Earthquake Seismogram (EQS) Denoiser–and two hybrid models processing both domains in parallel or sequentially. We evaluate waveform quality as a direct measure of denoising performance and assess the impact on signal detection and phase picking tasks using standard phase pickers. We further examine how denoising enhances signal onsets using a dedicated first‐motion polarity model, benchmark the best‐performing model against state‐of‐the‐art denoisers, and evaluate its generalization to out‐of‐distribution data. Our results show that the time‐domain model produces the most accurate waveforms at high signal‐to‐noise ratios (SNRs), but fails to detect event signals at low SNRs. The time‐frequency denoiser captures event signals down to lower SNRs but can introduce artifacts such as smeared onsets due to the time‐frequency binning. Hybrid models mitigate shortcomings of single‐domain approaches. The hybrid sequential model , which extends the EQS architecture, demonstrates strong signal detection at low SNRs while preserving sharp onsets, improving phase picking and extending first‐motion polarity determination to lower SNRs compared to raw or bandpass‐filtered data. Overall, surpasses benchmark models across every waveform and downstream task metric for both in‐ and out‐of‐distribution data, demonstrating that hybrid domain processing is a powerful strategy for accurate seismic denoising.

title: Bayesian Nonparametric Factor Analysis via Marginalized Dirichlet Process Column Clustering with Spike-and-Slab Sparsity
abstract: We propose a Bayesian nonparametric factor model that infers the number of factors, induces row-wise sparsity, and merges redundant dictionary elements via exact clustering. A Dirichlet process prior is placed on the columns of an overcomplete loading matrix and fully marginalized to an exact Pólya urn, avoiding stick-breaking and auxiliary variables. A spike-and-slab base measure allows entire factors to be exactly zero. The model uniquely combines exact zeros, exchangeability over columns, and exact merging within a single marginalized Dirichlet process, unlike CUSP, MGP, or the beta process. An exact Gibbs sampler with canonical relabeling and parallel C/MPI implementation is developed. We prove posterior contraction at rate $\sqrt{M s_0 \log n / n}$ for the covariance matrix, and in the fixed-dictionary setting obtain the minimax optimal rate $\sqrt{s_0 \log n / n}$ plus underfitting consistency; the overfitting direction is an open conjecture. The spike-and-slab is essential: without it the effective dimension scales as $pM$, yielding a slower rate. Simulations show the method is the only fully adaptive approach to recover the true rank, achieving the smallest covariance, loading, and signal-reconstruction errors, beating an oracle baseline. On van 't Veer breast cancer data ($n=97$, $p=1213$), the posterior concentrates on eight interpretable programmes; seven pass coherence and two pass Bonferroni-corrected Hallmark enrichment.

title: The Price of Self-Calibration: Exact Evidence Budgets and Manufactured Blind Sets in Adaptive Monitoring
abstract: Self-calibrating monitors adapt their threshold online to guarantee a prescribed long-run false-alarm rate under arbitrary drift. We compute the price of that guarantee, stating every law with its exact domain of validity. First, the guarantee is an accounting identity, insensitive to what the monitor is meant to detect. Two evidence identities make the cost exact for the online quantile tracker: a persistent step of height $δ$ yields excess alarm mass within one alarm of $δ/η$, and exactly $δ/η$ pathwise when $δ$ is a lattice multiple of the gain $η$; a ramp of slope $c$ yields a stationary excess rate of exactly $c/η$, independent of accumulated size, up to a boundary $c=η(1-α)$ coinciding with the alarm-rate cap. Second, the certificate's own fluctuation obeys an exact law: the windowed alarm rate has standard deviation of order $1/L$, not the binomial $1/\sqrt{L}$, since the windowed mass telescopes to a difference of a tight internal state; the closed-form constant is validated with no fitted parameter. Detectors calibrated on the binomial scale are miscalibrated by $\sqrt{η\varphi(q_0)L}$, and correct calibration turns detection windows from quadratic to linear in the inverse fault speed. Third, any monitor required to tolerate a drift class $\mathcal{D}$ is blind, at any horizon and for any rule, to every fault in $\mathcal{D}-\mathcal{D}$; the proof is a deliberately elementary two-point argument and the contribution is the object it identifies: for speed-bounded classes the blind set is exactly the doubled-speed class, and the tracker absorbs a speed class fixed by its own gain, so that under a certification regime declaring absorbed drift normal, the monitor manufactures $\mathcal{D}$. An exact Gaussian projection bound, sharper than Pinsker and never vacuous, quantifies power outside it.

title: Expert-Play Contouring Control: Faster-than-Demonstration Planning from Slow Expert and Fast Play
abstract: Expert demonstrations often specify what a robot should do, but not how fast it can do it. Imitation Learning (IL) inherits demonstration timing, while directly accelerating the learned motion can fail when faster execution changes the robot-object dynamics. We study faster-than-demonstration execution as a dynamics-aware control problem and introduce Expert-Play Contouring Control (EPCC), which combines slow expert demonstrations with fast, non-expert play. Expert demonstrations train a latent trajectory generator whose predictions are reparameterized into a time-independent contour of successful task progression, while play trains a world model (WM) of fast-action outcomes. At deployment, our proposed planner uses the WM to optimize actions that makes maximize progress along the expert-derived contour while penalizing deviation from the intended task evolution. Averaged across three visuomotor manipulation tasks, EPCC achieves a $2.0\times$ the throughput of the IL baseline, including $2.2\times$ that of the throughput of the strongest acceleration baseline on a task with interaction-sensitive object dynamics. Our analysis shows that the gains concentrate where faster execution changes robot-object evolution. Together, our results highlight a simple yet effective principle: demonstrations provide task intent, while play data provides the dynamic coverage needed to execute that intent faster.

At deployment, our proposed planner uses the WM to optimize actions that makes maximize progress along the expert-derived contour while penalizing deviation from the intended task evolution. Averaged across three visuomotor manipulation tasks, EPCC achieves a $2.0\times$ the throughput of the IL baseline, including $2.2\times$ that of the throughput of the strongest acceleration baseline on a task with interaction-sensitive object dynamics. Our analysis shows that the gains concentrate where faster execution changes robot-object evolution. Together, our results highlight a simple yet effective principle: demonstrations provide task intent, while play data provides the dynamic coverage needed to execute that intent faster.

title: StateMem: Single-State Residual Memory with Adaptive Inference for Vision-Language-Action Policies
abstract: Memory-dependent robotic manipulation often requires later actions to use information from earlier interactions. Existing vision-language-action (VLA) policies primarily rely on current observations, limiting historical information retention. Memory-augmented VLAs, such as MemoryVLA, address this limitation with external memory banks but require explicit storage and retrieval. To address these limitations, we propose StateMem, a single-state residual memory framework for VLA policies that uses prediction error to update a persistent memory token through low-rank residuals and to adaptively route cached prefixes. A training-free controller adjusts the routing threshold online, while fast correction compensates for stale prefix features during cache reuse. We evaluate StateMem on LIBERO, RoboMemArena, and real-world manipulation tasks. On LIBERO, StateMem achieves an average success rate of 97.6% and reduces the average VLM prefix refresh rate by 20.25% relative to full refresh. In the Occlusion category of RoboMemArena, StateMem achieves the best performance among single-VLA methods, reaching 21.8% Task Success Rate (TSR) and 44.3% Cumulative Success Rate (CSR). Across six real-world manipulation tasks, it achieves +21% in average success rate.

title: Применение сверточных нейронных сетей для автоматического выделения микросейсмических событий в данных локального мониторинга Северного Кавказа
abstract: Актуальность работы. Северный Кавказ характеризуется сложным геологическим строением, неоднородным сейсмическим фоном и влиянием природных и техногенных помех, что затрудняет автоматическое выделение слабых микросейсмических событий. Традиционные пороговые алгоритмы не всегда надежно обнаруживают низкоамплитудные сигналы, особенно при малом отношении сигнал/шум. Цель исследования. Оценить возможность применения сверточных нейронных сетей для автоматического обнаружения микросейсмических событий в трехкомпонентных записях локального мониторинга Северного Кавказа и сопоставить их эффективность с алгоритмом STA/LTA. Методы исследования.Использованы цифровые трехкомпонентные сейсмограммы локальных станций, прошедшие приведение к единой частоте дискретизации, полосовую фильтрацию, нормализацию и разделение на временные окна. Для классификации событий и шумовых фрагментов применялась одномерная CNN, анализирующая временные ряды по трем компонентам. Эффективность оценивалась по accuracy, recall, F1-мере и числу ложных срабатываний в сравнении с STA/LTA. Результаты. Наиболее устойчивые результаты получены для трехкомпонентных записей, окна 20 с, частоты 100 Гц и фильтрации 1–20 Гц. CNN обеспечила accuracy 0,93–0,95, recall 0,91–0,92 и F1-меру 0,92–0,93. По сравнению с STA/LTA модель лучше сохраняла баланс полноты обнаружения и ложных тревог, особенно при отношении сигнал/шум ниже 2,0. Результаты подтверждают перспективность CNN как модуля первичного обнаружения в системах сейсмического мониторинга Relevance. The North Caucasus is characterized by a complex geological structure, a heterogeneous seismic background, and natural and anthropogenic noise, which complicate automatic detection of weak microseismic events. Traditional threshold-based algorithms do not always reliably detect low-amplitude signals, especially under low signal-to-noise conditions. Aim of the study. The study aims to evaluate the use of convolutional neural networks for automatic detection of microseismic events in three-component local monitoring records from the North Caucasus and to compare their performance with the STA/LTA algorithm. Research methods. Digital three-component seismograms from local stations were resampled to a common sampling rate, bandpass filtered, normalized, and divided into time windows. A one-dimensional CNN was used to classify events and noise fragments by analyzing three-component time series. Performance was evaluated using accuracy, recall, F1-score, and the number of false alarms in comparison with STA/LTA. Results. The most stable results were obtained for three-component records, a 20 s window, a 100 Hz sampling rate, and 1–20 Hz filtering. The CNN achieved an accuracy of 0.93–0.95, recall of 0.91–0.92, and F1-score of 0.92–0.93. Compared with STA/LTA, the model provided a better balance between detection completeness and false alarms, especially at signal-to-noise ratios below 2.0. The results confirm the promise of CNN as a primary detection module in seismic monitoring systems

title: Inferring channel memory, phase, and noise symmetry from the output of noisy quantum teleportation
abstract: Abstract We consider quantum teleportation channels in which a phase $$\varphi$$ is imprinted onto the initial shared resource channel. The resource qudits interact with either two independent local environments or a common environment; we classify the noise as symmetric when the noise parameters on the two qudits are identical, and as asymmetric otherwise. By teleporting an arbitrary input state, we compute the Hilbert–Schmidt speed (HSS) and quantum Fisher information (QFI) of both the noisy resource channel and the teleported output state, each computed with respect to the initially encoded phase $$\varphi$$ . We show that under symmetric noise, the HSS and QFI of the teleported output reproduce the same qualitative temporal behavior as their resource-channel counterparts. Because HSS can witness essential non-Markovianity—defined here as the violation of P-divisibility—within established contractivity regimes, this correspondence enables indirect inference of the resource channel’s memory effects from the output alone, without requiring direct access to the channel after teleportation. The output HSS and QFI also carry information about the initial phase, allowing its estimation. We further find that asymmetric noise can cause the qualitative dynamics of the output HSS and QFI to deviate from those of the resource channel. Such a deviation provides a diagnostic signature of environmental asymmetry. HSS can be evaluated without diagonalizing the density matrix, making it practical for high-dimensional qudit teleportation; moreover, the output state has a lower dimension than the bipartite resource channel, offering a lower-dimensional probe that substantially reduces measurement and computational overhead. Within the representative noise models studied, these findings establish a unified framework for extracting information about channel memory, phase sensitivity, and noise symmetry directly from the accessible teleported output.

title: Genre-Routed Generative Resonance: Black-Box AI Text Detection via Dual-Horizon Probing and Structural Rhythm
abstract: Detecting text synthesized by frontier large language models (LLMs) remains a critical requirement for academic integrity, digital forensics, and media authenticity. Existing zero-shot detectors exhibit severe real-world failure modes: token-curvature methods (DetectGPT, Fast-DetectGPT) require inaccessible white-box model logits, while perplexity baselines disproportionately penalize non-native English writers. In our earlier investigations, single-branch cloze infilling collapsed when scaled to open-domain environments due to the Reasoning Prober Paradox, genre-dependent predictability asymmetry, the 1-word compound noun trap, and the brittleness of punctuation stylometry. This paper introduces Genre-Routed Generative Resonance (ClozeCongruence), a logit-free forensic framework that couples two complementary probing geometries via an automated linguistic Genre Router: factual and expository passages are directed to forward Prefix-Tail Completion, while creative and narrative prose is guided to middle-sentence Cloze Infilling. To shield human authors without punctuation counting, we formulate Clean Structural Dynamics, combining multi-pass inter-horizon void decay ($\Delta\text{void}$) with sentence-length coefficient of variation ($CV$). Across a balanced, stratified benchmark of $N = 1{,}000$ full-length documents (Academic Nature essays, Non-Native ESL essays, Wikipedia expository prose, Frontier LLMs including GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and LLaMA-3.3, and RAID adversarial evasions), three candidate architectures achieve reproducible discrimination with nonparametric bootstrap 95% confidence intervals and label-permutation tests ($p < 0.001$): (1) Clean Structural Geometric Fusion yields the highest global AUROC (0.8283, 95% CI [0.803, 0.853], Youden $J = 0.5120$), capturing 73.6% of frontier AI text at $\tau = 26\%$ with ESL FAR 10.0% and mean separation $+14.14\text{ pp}$ (human $20.29 \pm 8.33$, AI $34.43 \pm 14.57$). (2) Genre-Routed Hybrid with Two-Tier Gate provides a high-recall screening profile (79.8% TPR at $\tau = 26\%$; 69.8% TPR at Youden-optimal $\tau = 28\%$, AUROC 0.8184, 95% CI [0.791, 0.844], ESL FAR 9.0%). (3) Clean Structural Linear Fusion achieves the most conservative Youden-optimal ESL protection (8.5% FAR; AUROC 0.8107, 95% CI [0.783, 0.836]). At the enterprise disciplinary threshold ($\tau \ge 38\%$), Geometric Fusion yields 0.00% ESL false accusation (0/200); Two-Tier and Linear yield 0.5% and 1.0%, respectively. Code, cohorts, and audit logs are released for reproducibility.

title: Singular-Subspace Alignment in Norm-Constrained Asymmetric Low-Rank Updates
abstract: We study the singular-subspace geometry of an asymmetric low-rank update X=BA under a Frobenius-norm constraint. For the affine linearization of a smooth matrix loss, factorized first-order stationarity pairs singular subspaces of the gradient, while the factorized second-order condition selects the leading r subspaces exactly. For a nonlinear loss, let G and G̃ denote the gradients at the pretrained and adapted points. Under full-rank factors, an active constraint, a positive multiplier, and suitable spectral separation, we prove a Wedin-type bound: the alignment error is at most βc/δr(G,G̃), where β is the gradient-Lipschitz constant and c is the update budget. If βc<γG/4, this is bounded by 4βc/(3γG) relative to the pretrained gradient. Globally smooth constructions, including a convex one, attain the same asymptotic order. For r=1, exact alignment can fail outside this perturbative regime at a genuine factorized second-order stationary point. The results concern stationary-point geometry, not algorithmic convergence.

title: Cognitive Provenance - A Framework for the Traceable Formation and Evolution of Cognitive Assets
abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence is increasingly transforming cognitive production from a relatively linear process of individual knowledge creation into an iterative process involving human judgment, machine-assisted structuring, validation, transformation, and reuse. As cognitive outputs become continuously developed and recombined, the identity of a cognitive asset may no longer be adequately represented by its current expression alone. This Foundational Note introduces Cognitive Provenance as a conceptual layer within the broader Cognitive Property Theory (CPT) framework. Cognitive Provenance refers to the traceable history through which a cognitive asset is formed, contributed to, validated, transformed, and evolved. It extends the concept of cognitive asset beyond its current expression by treating the formation and evolution history of the asset as relevant to understanding its identity, continuity, and subsequent development. The central proposition is: A cognitive asset should be understood not only through its current expression, but also through a traceable provenance of its formation, contribution, validation, transformation, and evolution. Cognitive Provenance is distinguished from ordinary publication metadata, authorship attribution, intellectual property ownership, and legal priority. A DOI or other public record may provide a temporal or public provenance anchor, but does not by itself establish ownership, authorship, exclusivity, or enforceability. Cognitive Provenance is therefore proposed as a conceptual layer between Cognitive Assetization and the subsequent lifecycle, lineage, reuse, and organizational capability of cognitive assets. This Note does not propose a complete legal doctrine. It establishes a minimum conceptual claim for further development within CPT.

title: Integrated Deep Learning Framework Designed on Hybrid Optimization Strategies for Automated Health Detection and Analysis in Silkworms
abstract: A Hybrid Residual Attention Network is proposed for accurately classifying silkworm images into six different classes, including healthy and diseased states. It uses residual blocks for deep feature extraction and attention to focus on disease related features. A novel Integrated Adaptive Momentum Optimizer was introduced to enhance convergence and improve training efficiency. The dataset of silkworm images underwent preprocessing techniques such as normalization, resizing, and noise reduction, along with augmentation strategies to improve data quality and diversity. It is optimized using IAMO, achieved an accuracy of 98.67%.The integration of spatial and channel wise attention mechanisms, coupled with IAMO, significantly enhanced the model ability to recognize subtle differences between classes. Results indicate that HRAN can be used to detect disease at an early stage in sericulture, and future work will enhance scalability and efficiency in different environments.

title: Exact Quotients of Fresnel-Kummer Surfaces and Certified Biaxial Refraction
abstract: The Fresnel wave surface governs the propagation of light in a transparent biaxial crystal. It is a special Kummer quartic, and we identify it exactly. Over the complex numbers the wave surface of a crystal is the Kummer surface of the Jacobian of an explicit genus-two curve branched at the signed square roots of the three principal permittivities. This Jacobian is isogenous, by an isogeny with kernel of order four, to a product of two elliptic curves. One elliptic curve carries the three permittivities, and the other carries the optic-axis angle. The physical family is Zariski dense in the locus of genus-two curves with an extra involution, and its automorphism strata are explicit. The identification instantiates a task-aware quotient, which identifies parameters that differ by a nuisance transformation and carries invariant coordinates and explicit strata. For biaxial crystals, two ratios of the permittivities form a complete invariant of the wave surface up to rotation and rescaling, and the four real nodes are given in closed form. At an interface the candidate transmitted waves are the roots of a quartic of exact degree four. Its real-root count, root order, and repeated-root events are decided by exact algebraic predicates, and along the generic single-node encounters of the paper its discriminant vanishes to second order. Floating-point solvers drop forward transmitted modes near the optic axes, and the certified solver does not. On exact equivalence classes, learned models on quotient coordinates are invariant and more accurate than models on raw tensors, while learned root-count predicates fail near the optic axes.

title: "Dear LLaVA, Please Drive": A Depth-Aware Vision-Language Agent for Closed-Loop Robotic Control
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) provide a compelling foundation for reasoning-driven mobile navigation, offering rich contextual understanding and strong generalization from large-scale pretraining. Most existing navigation frameworks rely on imitation learning and therefore require substantial labeled trajectory data, limiting their scalability and robustness. In this work, we propose a parameter-efficient approach to fine-tune a pretrained VLM for autonomous navigation using an Imperative Learning paradigm. By optimizing against differentiable geometric cost fields rather than labeled trajectories, our model learns to generate collision-free paths exclusively from stereoscopic depth observations. We introduce a unified end-to-end navigation pipeline for natural-language-driven robotic control. This system leverages a shared VLM backbone with task-specific Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) modules, effectively bridging the gap from semantic target selection to low-level trajectory planning. Our approach achieves competitive Success weighted by Path Length (SPL) in unseen environments while updating less than 1% of the model's total parameters. Qualitative real-world experiments validate sim-to-real generalization and stable path planning without fine-tuning on real-world data. These results highlight a practical approach for deploying VLM-based agents on mobile robots, enabling high-level semantic navigation without the prohibitive requirement for large-scale, labeled trajectory data.

title: Mask-Aware Execution for Efficient JEPA Training
abstract: Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) are becoming a core representation-learning primitive and a building block for latent world models across vision, video, audio, brain dynamics, and time series. Despite (potential of) wide deployment, current JEPA training pipelines are inefficient: each input is executed through multiple mask-specific branches, with redundant target-side work, and memory-bound token routing. These costs grow with the number of masks and limit GPU efficiency. We present M-JEPA, a mask-aware execution architecture that restructures JEPA training without changing the learning objective. M-JEPA separates mask-independent computation from mask-dependent routing, enabling shared context encoder execution, fused token routing and slicing with backward support, sparse target encoder execution over the union of target tokens, and masked patch embedding for sparse inputs. The resulting pipeline preserves training semantics while reducing computation, memory traffic, and synchronization overhead. We implement M-JEPA for five JEPA variants and evaluate it on NVIDIA A100 GPUs. Compared against the state-of-the-art baselines, M-JEPA achieves up to 1.7x end-to-end training speedup for 2-10 masks. Separately, with masked patch embedding, 4.75x patch-embedding speedup at high sparsity. These results show that execution restructuring, rather than changes to the JEPA objective, is a key lever for efficient JEPA training.

title: Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning Models for Classification of Indonesian Texts
abstract: Text classification has become one of the fundamental tasks in Natural Language Processing (NLP) due to the rapid growth of unstructured textual data generated from digital platforms. Various Deep Learning models have been developed to improve classification performance; however, their effectiveness for Indonesian text classification remains a subject of investigation because of the unique linguistic characteristics of the Indonesian language. This study aims to compare the performance of four Deep Learning models, namely Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), and IndoBERT, for Indonesian text classification. The research employed an experimental quantitative approach using an Indonesian-language text dataset obtained from publicly available sources. Data preprocessing included case folding, text cleaning, tokenization, stopword removal, stemming, and text encoding before model training. The dataset was divided into 80% training data and 20% testing data. Model performance was evaluated using Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score, and Training Time. Experimental results showed that IndoBERT achieved the best performance with an accuracy of 96.48%, precision of 96.21%, recall of 96.08%, and F1-score of 96.14%, outperforming CNN, LSTM, and BiLSTM. Although IndoBERT required a longer training time, it demonstrated superior contextual understanding of Indonesian text through its Transformer-based architecture. The findings indicate that Transformer-based models provide higher classification performance than conventional Deep Learning models for Indonesian NLP tasks. This study offers valuable insights for researchers and practitioners in selecting appropriate Deep Learning models for sentiment analysis, document classification, fake news detection, and other Indonesian text processing applications.

title: Confidence-Driven Backdoor Poisoning in Text Classification: Sample Efficiency, Knowledge-Distillation Survival, and Defense Evasion Across Four Datasets
abstract: A backdoor attack hides a secret switch inside a machine learning model: the model behaves normally almost all the time, but produces an attacker-chosen wrong answer whenever a specific trigger appears in the input. The attacker installs the switch by corrupting a small number of training examples. A method called confidence-driven boundary sampling (CBS) proposes a smarter way to choose which examples to corrupt — pick the ones the model is already unsure about — and was shown on image classifiers to make the resulting backdoor harder for security checks to detect. CBS had never been evaluated on text, and nobody had checked whether these backdoors survive when a large model is compressed into a smaller one. We test both. We use BERT-base as the teacher and DistilBERT as the compressed student, two trigger families (a rare word and an out-of-domain sentence), and four datasets chosen so that each changes a single structural property: SST-2 (short text, binary) as the baseline, AG News (four classes), IMDB (long documents), and Yelp Polarity (long documents, different domain). We report four findings. First, CBS costs the attacker more, not less. To reach a 90% attack success rate on SST-2 it needs about 8.3 times more corrupted data than random selection (5 times for the sentence trigger); on Yelp's word trigger it never reaches 90% at all, even at twenty times random selection's budget. A three-seed replication confirms the SST-2 gap with non-overlapping variance. Second, compression removes most of the backdoor but never all of it. Retention spans 0.88–12.30% across the four datasets, even though the student is trained only on clean text; CBS retains more than random selection in 7 of 8 comparisons. Third, the stealth advantage CBS was designed for does not appear in text — and on Yelp it reverses. Three of four defenses barely affect either method on most datasets, and on Yelp's word trigger every defense strips substantially more from the CBS backdoor (3.9–18.8 points) than from the random one (≤0.2 points). Fourth, document length caps the attack, but the threshold is absolute rather than relative. IMDB plateaus at 79–86% and never reaches 90% at any rate from 0.02% to 10%. Yelp, also long-form, does not plateau — its typical document is 202.6 tokens against IMDB's 305.2. CBS selects systematically longer documents than random selection on both (300.5 vs. 202.6 on Yelp; 387.6 vs. 305.2 on IMDB), which places CBS-selected Yelp documents inside the same dilution regime IMDB imposes on every method — and explains why CBS alone fails on Yelp's word trigger. Code and per-run results: https://github.com/kannu74/cbs_on_text

title: N Logic Meta-Phase Space Reasoning Model
abstract: This paper proposes the N Logic Meta-Phase Space Reasoning Model (N-LMPS): on top of the single-layer logic meta-phase space (whose theory is given in Logic Meta-Phase Space Reasoning Model, hereafter the theory paper), it organizes two orthogonal axes and one review gate. (i) Resolution axis: a θ-refinement filtration C0→C1→⋯→CNC0→C1→⋯→CN of the same structure–symbol space (P,T) — multiple resolution views of one space, with nested partitions, a surjective fine-to-coarse projection ψ, and a canonical section φ satisfying ψ∘φ=id (Propositions 2.1/2.2/2.3); (ii) superposition axis: three classes of independent spaces defined by data source — a core space S₁ (trained on high-accuracy data, with safety specifications applied as application policy), generalization spaces S₂,…,S_M (further training data), and learning spaces S_{M+1},…,S_N (learning data from the usage process, which do not participate in reasoning directly) — combined as the √JS-fidelity-weighted superposition Q=∑iwiqiQ=∑iwiqi, wi∝exp⁡(−JS(qref∥qi))wi∝exp(−JS(qref∥qi)); (iii) review gate: learning content may be merged into the generalization spaces and thus participate in reasoning only after multi-round learning stability (absorption by reflection) and teacher-space answer confirmation (√JS fidelity ≤ θ_teacher). This paper provides the inter-layer maps, the cross-layer edge weights (projection consistency and refinement error), the promotion/demotion operators and their duality, the monotone bounded convergence of the potential function, the formalization and preservation of safety constraints, and three conduction theorems for superposition: Proposition 6.1 (one-step TV conduction), Proposition 6.3 (two-step JS and h² conductions), Proposition 6.4 (one-step Hellinger conduction plus an internal-spread term) — the deviation of the superposition is provably controlled by the fidelity-weighted average of its components, and the worst case never deteriorates. All conclusions are accompanied by basic validation (validation paper V1–V25). The authority of the core layer and the review thresholds are declared application policy: their formalization lies inside the theory, and the basis of their assignment lies outside it. Reading guide. §1.1 contains a self-contained review of the single-layer theory for readers without a logic-theory background; §1.5 summarizes the relation between the two axes and the validation correspondence; Appendix A gives the training and prediction flow diagrams; Appendix B gives a plain-language explanation; Appendix C gives a numerical mini-example. evidence.title: N Logic Meta-Phase Space Reasoning Model
evidence.abstract: This paper proposes the N Logic Meta-Phase Space Reasoning Model (N-LMPS): on top of the single-layer logic meta-phase space (whose theory is given in Logic Meta-Phase Space Reasoning Model, hereafter the theory paper), it organizes two orthogonal axes and one review gate. (i) Resolution axis: a θ-refinement filtration C0→C1→⋯→CNC0→C1→⋯→CN of the same structure–symbol space (P,T) — multiple resolution views of one space, with nested partitions, a surjective fine-to-coarse projection ψ, and a canonical section φ satisfying ψ∘φ=id (Propositions 2.1/2.2/2.3); (ii) superposition axis: three classes of independent spaces defined by data source — a core space S₁ (trained on high-accuracy data, with safety specifications applied as application policy), generalization spaces S₂,…,S_M (further training data), and learning spaces S_{M+1},…,S_N (learning data from the usage process, which do not participate in reasoning directly) — combined as the √JS-fidelity-weighted superposition Q=∑iwiqiQ=∑iwiqi, wi∝exp⁡(−JS(qref∥qi))wi∝exp(−JS(qref∥qi)); (iii) review gate: learning content may be merged into the generalization spaces and thus participate in reasoning only after multi-round learning stability (absorption by reflection) and teacher-space answer confirmation (√JS fidelity ≤ θ_teacher).
